title: Sell Mineral Rights in Petrolia, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Petrolia, PA
metaDescription: Petrolia, PA mineral rights owner in historic Butler County oil country? We buy legacy shallow and modern Marcellus interests, cash offers, no pressure.
heroLead: Petrolia earned its name honestly — this was one of the boom towns of Pennsylvania's original 1870s oil rush, not far from where the industry itself got its start near Titusville, and the mineral rights under this ground carry more layered history than almost anywhere else we work.
intro: If your family has held minerals near Petrolia for generations, you may be sitting on rights that were first leased during the shallow oil boom of the 1870s and 80s, then possibly re-leased decades later for deeper Marcellus development. Untangling which rights are still active, which old wells have been plugged and abandoned, and what's actually available to sell today takes real title work, and it's exactly the kind of history we take seriously rather than skip past.

sections.heading: Layers of Ownership From the Original Oil Boom
paragraphs: Petrolia's shallow wells from the 19th century are mostly long depleted, and many were plugged decades ago, but that doesn't mean the mineral rights themselves lost value — deeper Marcellus rights under the same acreage are a separate asset, and Butler County has seen real modern wet-gas activity in surrounding townships. We check both the historical shallow record and current deep leasing activity before quoting a number.

Because this area's oil history is so old, some deeds reference wells, leases, or reservations using language and boundary descriptions that don't match modern surveys. We work through those older instruments carefully so your offer reflects what you actually own today.

sections.heading: What We Look at Before Making an Offer
paragraphs: We pull the recorded chain of title from the Butler County recorder of deeds, confirm whether your interest is currently under an active Marcellus lease, and check proximity to producing units nearby. Any figure we give you is a range tied to that activity, since Petrolia-area tracts vary a lot depending on how close they sit to current drilling.

faqs.question: My deed mentions an oil lease from the 1800s. Does that still matter?
faqs.answer: Usually the original shallow lease is long expired or the well plugged, but the underlying mineral rights are still yours to sell or lease for deeper Marcellus development. We check the full history.

faqs.question: Are there still active shallow wells near Petrolia?
faqs.answer: Some legacy shallow wells remain in the area, though most historic Petrolia-era wells have been plugged. Current activity is mostly tied to deeper Marcellus development.

faqs.question: How do I know if I still hold both shallow and deep rights?
faqs.answer: We trace the recorded deed history to confirm exactly what depths and rights you hold before making an offer.
